alt: A formula triangle with m on top and ρ and V below gives ρ = m/V, m = ρV and V = m/ρ. Beside it, kilograms with cubic metres give kg/m³ and grams with cubic centimetres give g/cm³, and 1 g/cm³ = 0.001 ÷ 0.000 001 = 1000 kg/m³; water is about 1.0 g/cm³ or 1000 kg/m³.
caption: ρ = m/V, with mass and volume in matching units; 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³.

alt: A copper block of mass m and volume V is cut into two halves. Each half has mass m/2 and volume V/2, so its density (m/2) ÷ (V/2) is still m/V.
caption: Halving mass and volume together leaves the density unchanged.

alt: A concrete slab 0.60 m by 0.40 m by 0.050 m with density 2400 kg/m³. Its volume is 0.012 m³, its mass 2400 × 0.012 = 28.8 kg and its weight 28.8 × 9.8 = 282 N.
caption: Find the volume in m³ first, then m = ρV, then W = mg.

alt: Left: a brass cuboid 5.0 cm by 3.0 cm by 2.0 cm on a balance reading 255 g; V = 30 cm³ and ρ = 255/30 = 8.5 g/cm³ = 8500 kg/m³. Right: an empty measuring cylinder reads 86.4 g and 126.4 g with 50.0 cm³ of liquid, so the liquid has mass 40.0 g and density 0.800 g/cm³.
caption: Volume from a ruler or a measuring cylinder; mass from a balance; then ρ = m/V.

alt: Method A: a stone on a thread is lowered into a part-filled measuring cylinder and its volume is the rise in the reading. Method B: the stone is lowered into a full displacement can and the water that runs out of the spout into a measuring cylinder equals its volume. Precautions are listed below.
caption: The object's volume is the rise in level, or the volume of water pushed out.

alt: A tank of water of density 1.0 g/cm³. Ice (0.92 g/cm³) and a pine block (0.50 g/cm³) float, while brass (8.5 g/cm³) and plastic of density 1.2 g/cm³ rest on the bottom.
caption: An object floats if it is less dense than the liquid and sinks if it is denser.

alt: A jar holds three liquids that do not mix: Y (0.86 g/cm³) on top, water (1.00 g/cm³) in the middle and X (1.26 g/cm³) at the bottom. A bead of density 0.95 g/cm³ sinks through Y but floats on the water, so it rests at the Y–water boundary.
caption: Layers stack in order of density; an object settles between a less dense and a denser liquid.
